answer: Downregulation of genes primarily drives the metabolic effects of CBD treatment in CRC cells. In the primary contrast (CBD_IC50 vs DMSO vehicle), 108 genes are significantly down-regulated versus 58 up-regulated (padj < 0.05, BH, and |log2FC| > 0.5), and the down-regulated set carries the larger total effect (sum of log2FC: −79.0 for down vs +47.7 for up; median −0.66 vs +0.66, i.e., down-regulated hits are also slightly larger in magnitude on average). A Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the log2FC values of all significant primary genes confirms a significant shift toward negative fold changes (p = 0.0013). The direction imbalance holds even before the padj filter (|log2FC| > 0.5: 753 down vs 560 up). The serum-starvation sensitivity contrast (CBD_IC50+SS16h vs DMSO+SS16h) shows the same pattern, more strongly: 934 down vs 711 up significant genes, total effect −889 vs +615 log2FC units (Wilcoxon p = 1.3e-11), and 108 genes are significant in both contrasts with 106/108 agreeing in direction. Thus, across both contrasts and every quantification (gene counts, median and mean log2FC, cumulative effect size, distributional test), CBD's transcriptional response in these CRC cells is dominated by gene down-regulation, indicating that suppression (rather than activation) of gene expression programs is the primary driver of CBD's metabolic effects. Caveat: GO Biological Process over-representation enrichment (separate up/down runs vs the pre-filtered universe, BH-corrected) could not be executed because the runner has no internet access, no R/clusterProfiler or gseapy/mygene installation, and no local GO annotation resources (no GMT/OBO/gene2go files anywhere on disk); this limitation is documented in the analysis log and no enrichment results were fabricated. The direction-of-effect conclusion rests on the differential expression evidence, which is unambiguous and consistent across both approved contrasts.
